table.name: car_makers
table.purpose: One row per automobile manufacturer; links each maker to its home country and is referenced by model_list which lists its car models.

Country.name: country_id
Country.description: Foreign key to countries.CountryId identifying the maker's home country (e.g. 2=germany, 4=japan, 7=uk).

FullName.name: full_name
FullName.description: Manufacturer's full official name (e.g. 'American Motor Company', 'General Motors'), unique per row.

Id.name: maker_id
Id.description: Primary key of the car maker; referenced by model_list.Maker to associate models with their manufacturer.

Maker.name: maker_name
Maker.description: Short/lowercase maker name (e.g. 'gm', 'bmw', 'fiat'), unique per row; the one_to_one join to model_list.Model is likely coincidental value overlap rather than a true reference.

table.name: car_names
table.purpose: Maps each car model name (make + model string) to an ID, linking the maker (Model) to the model_list table and serving as the referenced key for cars_data specifications. One row per distinct car model name.

Make.name: model_name
Make.description: Full car model name combining manufacturer and model, e.g. 'ford pinto', 'audi 4000'. Not unique (same name can appear for different years/variants).

MakeId.name: car_model_id
MakeId.description: Primary key; unique ID for each car model name (1-406). Referenced by cars_data, which presumably stores per-car specifications keyed by this ID.

Model.name: maker_name
Model.description: Manufacturer/make name (e.g. 'ford', 'chevrolet'), despite the column name 'Model'. References model_list.Model, linking each car to its maker.

table.name: cars_data
table.purpose: Per-car technical specifications (the classic 'auto-mpg' style dataset): one row per car model/record with fuel economy, engine and performance attributes, 1970-1982 model years.

Accelerate.name: Acceleration (0-60 mph time)
Accelerate.description: Time to accelerate, in seconds (range 8.0-24.8, mean ~15.5); consistent with 0-60 mph acceleration times for 1970s cars.

Cylinders.name: Number of engine cylinders
Cylinders.description: Engine cylinder count; values 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, dominated by 4 (207) and 8 (108).

Edispl.name: Engine displacement
Edispl.description: Engine displacement in cubic inches (cu in); range 68-455, values like 350, 318, 400, 455 match common US engine displacements. Could also be read as cc, but 455 cc is implausible for a car while 455 cu in (e.g. Oldsmobile 455) is well attested.

Horsepower.name: Engine horsepower
Horsepower.description: Engine power in horsepower, stored as text; range 46-230. The detected join to car_names.MakeId is spurious (statistical coincidence), as horsepower is a measure, not a key.

Id.name: Row identifier
Id.description: Primary key; sequential integer 1-406 identifying each car record.

MPG.name: Fuel economy (miles per gallon)
MPG.description: Fuel consumption in miles per gallon, stored as text; range 9.0-46.6, mean ~23.5, typical of 1970s-80s cars.

Weight.name: Vehicle weight
Weight.description: Curb weight in pounds; range 1613-5140 lbs, consistent with 1970s passenger cars.

Year.name: Model year
Year.description: Model year of the car, 1970-1982 (13 distinct years).

table.name: continents
table.purpose: Lookup table of the five continents; referenced by countries.Continent to assign each country to a continent.

ContId.name: continent_id
ContId.description: Primary key; numeric identifier for each continent (1-5). Referenced by countries.Continent.

Continent.name: continent_name
Continent.description: Name of the continent: america, europe, asia, africa, australia.

table.name: countries
table.purpose: Lookup table of countries (15 rows), each with its continent; referenced by car_makers to indicate a maker's home country.

Continent.name: continent_id
Continent.description: Foreign key to continents.ContId; identifies the continent the country belongs to (1=america, 2=europe, 3=asia, 4=africa, 5=australia).

CountryId.name: country_id
CountryId.description: Primary key; unique numeric identifier of the country, referenced by car_makers.Country.

CountryName.name: country_name
CountryName.description: Unique lowercase name of the country (e.g. germany, japan, uk, new zealand).

table.name: model_list
table.purpose: Maps each car model (brand name) to its maker (car manufacturer), linking models to the car_makers table. One row per distinct car model/make name.

Maker.name: maker_id
Maker.description: Foreign key to car_makers.Id identifying the manufacturer of the model (e.g. 4 = General Motors, 13 = Daimler Benz).

Model.name: model_name
Model.description: Car make/model name (e.g. 'buick', 'mercedes-benz', 'opel'). Unique per row; referenced by car_names.Model to link individual named cars to their model.

ModelId.name: model_id
ModelId.description: Primary key of the table; unique numeric identifier for each model, values 1-36.
